text: London's river smelled so bad, Parliament hung curtains soaked in chemicals. It was eighteen fifty eight. The river was full of raw sewage, in a very hot summer. Disraeli called it a stygian pool, reeking with intolerable horrors. Parliament quickly passed a bill for new sewers. Engineer Joseph Bazalgette built about eighty miles of them. Part of that system still serves London today. It took a terrible smell to make politicians act. Would you have stayed in the room?
